name: Nitroglycerin
summary: At Bael Modan, Nitroglycerin helps the dwarves drive their excavation through tauren lands. Their soldiers and officers carry the volatile chemical, which can also be used against the fortress.

sections.title: Industrial Demolition
sections.body: Bael Modan's dwarves dig into the ancestral lands of the Stonespire tauren with heavy drillers and volatile chemicals. At the excavation site and its fortified keep, they keep nitroglycerin close to blast deep holes and break apart hills. Soldiers and officers, including Lord Cyrik Blackforge, carry vials of the fluid as the digging continues.

sections.title: A Taste of Their Own Medicine
sections.body: After Prospector Khazgorm dies, Gann Stonespire seeks to destroy the encroaching fortress. The displaced tauren brave studies dwarven engineering plans and learns that nitroglycerin combined with wood pulp and sodium nitrate makes a charge strong enough to strike Bael Modan's military garrison.

faq.answer: Dwarven forces at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens carry nitroglycerin, including Bael'dun Soldiers, Riflemen, Officers, and Lord Cyrik Blackforge in the keep.

faq.q: What is the nitroglycerin used for?
faq.answer: Gann Stonespire combines nitroglycerin with wood pulp and sodium nitrate to make a powerful charge against the military fortress at Bael Modan.

faq.q: Why were the dwarves carrying it in the first place?
faq.answer: The Bael Modan prospectors and garrison use explosives, steam engines, and volatile chemicals to open the earth at their archaeological dig site.
Gann Stonespire is an exiled tauren warrior whose tribe lost its ancestral lands when the dwarves built the Bael Modan excavation site and keep, driving them out through industrial destruction.

angles.text: Engineers know nitroglycerin as a compounding explosive. Wood pulp absorbs it, and sodium nitrate helps make it stable and detonable.
As a tauren, you know the volatile chemicals around Bael Modan as a bitter mark of the destruction inflicted on the Stonespire tribe.
